Elaine: Heads up — during a sustained multi-tenant stress run on staging I saw a sharp P95 regression on kv eviction paths for shard 17. P95 jumped from ~120ms to ~2.3s for a 20 minute window starting ~3967890000. Logs attached below.

Chris: Can you paste the shard config and the exact pressures you saw? Did the autoscaler or threshold step recently?

Elaine: Config snippet: `policy: LRU
hotset_threshold: 0.78
cooldown_ms: 5000
batch_size_hint: 64`
Sample log line: `evict: shard=17 pressure=0.92 threshold=0.78 policy=LRU reused=0.03 reinserts=4123 loop_ms=18.4`

Devon: Interesting — I repro'd locally with `./tools/kv-repro --shard=17 --qps=1100 --ctx-len=4096` and profiling shows evicter loop taking most CPU. `perf top` hotspots: 48% in `evicter::process_reinsert`, 21% in `memmove`, 12% in `kv::finalize_entry`.

Ryan: Did you try toggling policy to FIFO for the same workload? FIFO has been less aggressive on reuse churn in some prior tests.

Elaine: I ran a quick canary switching policy->FIFO on one staging replica. P95 dropped to ~180ms during the same run, throughput steady. But we observed a correctness warning: occasional `kv_pointer_mismatch` traces while the FIFO canary was up.

Susan: That matches an older bug where FIFO reinsert ordering exposed stale index windows under concurrent readers. We fixed the correctness postmortem last year but maybe this path regressed. We need to verify no correctness tradeoff.

Chris: Can you share the repro command and the minimal log snippet for the mismatch?

Elaine: Repro command: `./tools/kv-repro --shard=17 --qps=1200 --maxlen=8192 --duration=600`
Mismatch snippet: `WARN kv: shard=17 id=0x8f2 ptr=0x7ffef123 stale=true expected_epoch=42 actual_epoch=39 caller=read_path`

Devon: I dug into the trace. The root cause looks like reinserts happening while a background compact moves entries; our reinsertion fast-path increments the slot epoch but a racing reader can still observe the old pointer if CAS ordering isn't strict. LRU triggers more reinserts which amplifies the race.

Ryan: So LRU bias causes reinserts -> more write-side churn -> exposes epoch race. With FIFO we reduce reinserts but hit the legacy ordering bug. Both bad.

Susan: Short-term mitigation: add a serialized fence around reinsert+epoch bump and increase threshold to reduce churn. Try `hotset_threshold = 0.85` and `evicter_fence = true` on a canary. That should reduce reinserts and close the race.

Elaine: Did that. Canary patch (build 2026.3.9-canary) applied to one replica: results: reinserts dropped ~8x, P95 back to 140ms, and no mismatch warnings in a 30m run. CPU for evicter dropped 60% in `perf top`.

Chris: Nice. Can you post the exact metrics diff (reinserts/sec, P95, CPU) and attach flamegraphs? We'll need this for the postmortem and for deciding whether to upstream the fence as permanent.

Elaine: Metrics (canary vs baseline): `reinserts/sec: 520 -> 64`, `P95: 2300ms -> 140ms`, `evicter CPU%: 48% -> 18%`. Flamegraph links: https://perf.redwood/staging/fg/396789/evicter-canary and https://perf.redwood/staging/fg/396789/evicter-baseline

Devon: The fence fix looks safe but adds a tiny latency on rare hits. We should run correctness fuzz across longer contexts (16k+) to ensure no regressions. Also add unit tests covering concurrent reinsert+compact.

Ryan: Proposal: 1) ship fence + raised threshold as emergency mitigations to staging and then prod in two-step rollout, 2) add FIFO vs LRU benchmark harness to our nightly perf matrix, 3) schedule a deeper code-level review and a postmortem to capture root cause and long-term design (maybe a tiered-evict strategy).

Susan: Agreed. I'll open issues: `#ISSUE-evict-race-396789` for correctness follow-up and `#ISSUE-evict-mitigation-396789` for rollout. Assigning to Devon for code changes and to Elaine for perf verification.

evicter-bot: Deploy event: rollout/evict-fence-canary -> staging-17 succeeded (build 2026.3.9-canary). See traces: https://traces.redwood/3967890123

Elaine: Next steps: run 6-hour long fuzz with `--maxlen=16384` and collect full traces + flamegraphs, then escalate to prod canary if stable. I'll update the issues with results tomorrow. :eyes:

Chris: Thanks team. Great catch and quick mitigation. :thumbsup:
